definition_zh: 突袭；突击搜查；突袭行动；挖角
definition_en: a sudden short attack; a sudden visit by police looking for something; to attack or search a place suddenly; an attempt to take staff or business from a rival
core_image: 天未亮时几辆无标志的车同时停在仓库门口
scene: 天还没亮，几辆没有标志的车停在仓库门口，车门同时打开。 Police raided the warehouse before dawn and seized the records.
sceneCN: 这里 raid 是「突袭、突击搜查」（第 3 个义项：突然进入某处搜查或攻击）；句意为警方在黎明前突击搜查了那座仓库并带走了记录。画面里可留意：同时打开的车门、仓库的卷帘门、被带走的一箱文件。

pos.zh: 突袭；突击搜查；（商业）挖角

collocations.zh: 企业挖角；企业收购突袭

derivatives.zh: raid 加 -er，指实施突袭者，也指挖角或收购的机构
raid 加 -ing，指突袭或挖角这一行为
air 与 raid 复合，指从空中发动的袭击

senses.title: A sudden short attack
senses.definition: a brief and sudden attack on a place, especially in wartime
senses.definitionCN: 对某地发动的短暂而突然的攻击，尤指战时
senses.example: The raid destroyed two supply depots.
senses.exampleCN: 那次突袭摧毁了两座补给仓库。
senses.why: The word goes back to an old word for a riding or a journey, and an armed ride into enemy land became the raid.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到表示「骑马出行」的古老词，一次骑马闯入敌境的行动就成了 raid。

senses.title: A sudden police search
senses.definition: a surprise visit by police or officials to search a place
senses.definitionCN: 警方或官员为搜查某处而进行的突然到访
senses.example: Police carried out a raid on the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 警方对那座仓库进行了突击搜查。
senses.why: A search that arrives without warning borrows the military image of a sudden attack.
senses.whyCN: 不打招呼就到达的搜查借用了「突然袭击」这一军事形象。

senses.title: To attack or search suddenly
senses.definition: to enter a place suddenly in order to attack it or to look for something
senses.definitionCN: 为攻击或搜寻某物而突然进入某处
senses.example: Officers raided the office at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 警官们在黎明时突击搜查了那间办公室。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, so the action of making a raid is simply to raid.
senses.whyCN: 名词化为动词，实施一次突袭的动作就直接叫 raid。

senses.title: An attempt to take from a rival
senses.definition: an attempt to take a rival's staff, customers or business in one move
senses.definitionCN: 一次性地夺走对手的员工、客户或业务的行为
senses.example: The bank's raid on rival staff caused a scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行挖走对手员工的事引发了一场丑闻。
senses.why: Business borrowed the military word for a swift move against a rival, and the sense of taking by surprise carried over.
senses.whyCN: 商界借用了这个军事词，指对对手采取的迅速行动，其中「出其不意地夺取」的意味也一并带了过来。

intro.en: Raid is a northern English word for a riding or a journey, related to ride and road; the military sense grew from an armed ride into enemy country.
intro.cn: raid 是英格兰北部表示「骑马出行」的词，与 ride、road 同源；军事义从一次武装骑马进入敌国生长出来。

items.en: Rad meant a riding, a journey or a road, and it is the common ancestor of several travelling words.
items.cn: rad 意为骑行、行程或道路，是好几个与出行有关的词的共同祖先。

items.en: The northern form raid kept the sense of a mounted journey when southern English said road.
items.cn: 北方的形式 raid 保留了「骑马出行」的意思，而南方英语说 road。

items.en: Raids across the Scottish border were mounted journeys ending in plunder, and the word took on the attack itself.
items.cn: 越过苏格兰边境的突袭是以劫掠收尾的骑马行程，这个词于是转指攻击本身。

items.en: Air raid and police raid extended the same sudden-move image to the sky and to law enforcement.
items.cn: 空袭与警方突击搜查把同一个「突然行动」的形象扩展到天空与执法领域。

items.en: Modern English also uses raid for a business move that takes staff or customers from a rival.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 raid 指从对手那里夺走员工或客户的商业行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same travelling root; the near-meaning group gathers words for sudden attacks and searches.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出行」词根上的形式；近义组收表示突然袭击与搜查的词。

entries.definition: A person or group that carries out a raid.
The activity of making raids.
To sit on and control a moving animal or vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 骑乘并控制移动的动物或车辆。

entries.definition: A prepared way for travelling between places.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两地、供出行使用的道路。

entries.definition: A violent act against a person or place.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或地方的暴力行为。

entries.definition: A careful look through a place for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为寻找某物而仔细查看一个地方。

entries.definition: A sudden entry into another's territory.
A sudden downward movement to seize something.
entries.definitionCN: 突然俯冲下来抓取某物。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a riding and became a sudden attack; the same picture of a fast move explains the police raid and the business raid.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「骑马出行」开始，变成突然袭击；同一幅「快速行动」的画面解释了警方搜查与商业挖角。

normal.en: Raid, ride and road come from one old word for a journey, which is why a raid feels like a fast trip with a purpose.
normal.cn: raid、ride 与 road 同出一个表示行程的古老词，所以 raid 感觉像一次有目的的快速出行。

normal.en: An air raid comes from the sky, while a police raid comes through the door.
normal.cn: 空袭从天上来，警方突击从门口进。

normal.en: Carry out a raid is the standard phrase for the police action, used with the noun rather than the verb.
normal.cn: carry out a raid 是描述警方行动的标准说法，用名词而不用动词。

normal.en: A raider is the person or group that raids, and raiding is the activity itself.
normal.cn: raider 是实施突袭的人或团体，raiding 则是这项活动本身。

normal.en: A corporate raid takes staff or a business from a rival in one swift move.
normal.cn: corporate raid 指以一次迅速行动从对手那里夺走员工或业务。

abstract.en: A raid assumes that surprise is worth more than preparation, and sometimes it is.
abstract.cn: 突袭假定出其不意比充分准备更有价值，有时确实如此。

abstract.en: The same word covers a soldier, a policeman and a headhunter, because all three arrive without warning.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指士兵、警察，也指挖角者，因为三者都不打招呼就到来。

abstract.en: What a raid takes is often less important than what it makes the defender feel.
abstract.cn: 突袭夺走的东西，往往不如它让被袭者感受到的更重要。

examples.en: The village was warned about the raid an hour before it began.
examples.cn: 突袭开始前一小时，村子就得到了警告。

examples.en: Customs officers raided the shop and found the missing goods.
examples.cn: 海关人员突击检查了这家店，找到了失踪的货物。

examples.en: The airline accused its rival of raiding its pilots.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司指责对手挖走它的飞行员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐的」——一支锐利的队伍突然冲进去，记住 raid 是突袭。

root: 古英语 rad（骑行、行程）→ 北方方言 raid → 英语 raid；同族有 ride、road、raider。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sudden armed move; the senses divide into a wartime attack, a police search, the act of doing it, and a business move against a rival.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「突然的武装行动」；义项分为战时攻击、警方搜查、实施这一行动，以及针对对手的商业动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: unmarked cars stopping at a warehouse gate before daylight.
core.cn: 核心意象：天未亮时几辆无标志的车停在仓库门口。

branches.en: a gate forced open in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗中撬开的门

branches.en: drawers emptied onto a table
branches.cn: 抽屉里的东西被倒到桌上

branches.en: a door opened at exactly the same second
branches.cn: 在同一秒打开的一扇扇车门

branches.en: a rival's best staff leaving together
branches.cn: 对手最好的员工一起离开

branches.en: the same surprise, once meant to destroy and once to find
branches.cn: 同一种出其不意，一次为破坏，一次为查找

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its relatives are made with English endings and compounds rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族短词，其亲属词靠英语词尾与复合方式构成，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

items.meaning: a business move against a rival

definition_zh: 为……配备家具；提供；供应
definition_en: to put furniture in a room or building, or to provide something that is needed
core_image: 空房间里摆上了床、桌子和椅子
scene: 这套公寓配了几件简单的家具。 The flat is furnished with a few simple pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 furnish 是「配备家具」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这套公寓配了几件简单的家具。

senses.title: Put furniture in
senses.definition: to put furniture and equipment into a room or building
senses.definitionCN: 把家具和设备放进房间或建筑物
senses.example: The flat is furnished with a few simple pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓配了几件简单的家具。
senses.why: This is the everyday housing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常居住场景中的义项。

senses.title: Provide information
senses.definition: to give someone information or evidence they need
senses.definitionCN: 给出别人需要的信息或证据
senses.example: The report furnishes useful information.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告提供了有用的信息。
senses.why: Supplying facts is like supplying furniture.
senses.whyCN: 提供事实就像提供家具一样。

senses.title: Supply materials
senses.definition: to supply a place or person with goods or materials
senses.definitionCN: 向某地或某人供应货物或材料
senses.example: They furnished the hall for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼布置并供应了大厅所需的物品。
senses.why: The older sense covers any needed supply.
senses.whyCN: 较早的义项涵盖任何所需的供应。

intro.en: Furnish came from an Old French verb meaning to provide.
intro.cn: furnish 来自一个意为「提供」的古法语动词。

items.en: Furnir meant to provide or complete.
items.cn: furnir 意为提供或完成。

items.en: The word first meant to supply.
items.cn: 这个词最初意为供应。

items.en: It came to mean fitting out a room.
items.cn: 它逐渐指为房间配置家具。

items.en: It also means supplying facts and evidence.
items.cn: 它也指提供事实和证据。

items.en: Furnished flats became common in cities.
items.cn: 带家具的公寓在城市里变得普遍。

note.en: Furnish is compared with look-alike words and words for supplying.
note.cn: 把 furnish 与形近词以及表示供应的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bring something to an end
a chamber of great heat
movable household goods
to supply with needed things
to provide what is needed
to give something to someone

normalIntro.en: To furnish is to fill a place or a need.
normalIntro.cn: furnish 就是填满一个地方或满足一种需要。

normal.en: The flat is furnished with a few simple pieces.
normal.cn: 这套公寓配了几件简单的家具。

normal.en: The report furnishes useful information.
normal.cn: 这份报告提供了有用的信息。

normal.en: They furnished the hall for the wedding.
normal.cn: 他们为婚礼布置并供应了大厅所需的物品。

normal.en: The landlord furnishes every room with a desk.
normal.cn: 房东给每个房间配一张书桌。

normal.en: He furnished proof of his address.
normal.cn: 他提供了住址证明。

abstract.en: A mind is furnished by the books it keeps.
abstract.cn: 一个人的心智由他收藏的书来布置。

abstract.en: Kindness furnishes a room better than gold.
abstract.cn: 善意比黄金更能装点一个房间。

abstract.en: What we supply to others furnishes our own character.
abstract.cn: 我们供给别人的东西也在塑造自己的品格。

examples.en: The flat is furnished with a few simple pieces.
examples.cn: 这套公寓配了几件简单的家具。

examples.en: The report furnishes useful information.
examples.cn: 这份报告提供了有用的信息。

examples.en: He furnished proof of his address.
examples.cn: 他提供了住址证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: furnish 与 finish 只差一个字母；furnish a room 是「布置房间」，furnish evidence 是「提供证据」。

root: 经古法语 furnir（提供）进入英语，核心义「把所需之物供给到位」。

sensesIntro.en: Furnish means fitting a room with furniture, giving information, or supplying goods.
sensesIntro.cn: furnish 指给房间配家具、提供信息，或供应货物。

core.en: To fill a space or a need with what it requires.
core.cn: 用所需之物填满空间或需求。

branches.en: Tables and chairs fill an empty room.
branches.cn: 桌椅填满空房间。

branches.en: A report supplies needed facts.
branches.cn: 报告提供需要的事实。

branches.en: Goods are sent to a place in need.
branches.cn: 货物被送往有需要的地方。

branches.en: Furniture is a kind of supply.
branches.cn: 家具也是一种供应品。

branches.en: Information furnishes the mind.
branches.cn: 信息装点着心智。

intro.en: Furnish builds words for fitting out and supplying.
intro.cn: furnish 构成表示布置和供应的词。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Old French rather than straight from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经古法语传来，而非直接来自拉丁语。

items.example: They will furnish the office this week.
items.exampleCN: 他们这周会给办公室配家具。

items.example: The guide furnishes maps and advice.

items.exampleCN: 我们租了一套带家具的公寓。

items.example: Furnishing the house took a month.
items.exampleCN: 布置这所房子花了一个月。

items.example: The furnisher delivered the desks on time.
items.exampleCN: 供应商按时送来了书桌。

items.example: The unfurnished room echoed when we spoke.
items.exampleCN: 没家具的房间说话都有回声。
他们重新布置了那家老酒店。

items.example: The library is well-furnished and quiet.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆家具齐全又安静。

definition_zh: 方程式；等式；复杂局面
definition_en: a mathematical statement that two things are equal, or a set of factors to balance
core_image: 等号两边放着同样多的东西，必须保持平衡
scene: 老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。 The teacher asked a student to solve a simple equation on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 equation 是「方程式」（第 1 个义项：数学中用等号连接两边的式子）；句意：老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。

collocations.phrase: the other side of the equation

senses.title: A mathematical equation
senses.definition: a mathematical statement showing that two expressions are equal
senses.definitionCN: 表明两个表达式相等的数学陈述
senses.example: This equation has two possible answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有两个可能的解。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to make equal, so it names a statement of equality.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自意为「使相等」的拉丁动词，因此指一个表示相等的陈述。

senses.title: A chemical equation
senses.definition: a symbolic statement that balances the atoms on each side of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用符号表示反应两边原子数平衡的式子
senses.example: The class balanced the chemical equation together.
senses.exampleCN: 全班一起配平了这个化学方程式。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the equal-sign form to show that matter is conserved.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用等号形式来表示物质守恒。

senses.title: A set of factors to balance
senses.titleCN: 复杂局面；需权衡的因素
senses.definition: a situation in which several factors must be weighed together
senses.definitionCN: 必须把多个因素放在一起权衡的情形
senses.example: Cost is only one part of the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 成本只是需要权衡的因素之一。
senses.why: If an equation balances two sides, a real situation can be pictured as sides to weigh.
senses.whyCN: 如果方程要平衡两边，现实局面也可以被想象成需要权衡的两边。

intro.en: Equation comes from Latin aequatio, a making equal, from aequare, to make level, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equation 来自拉丁语 aequatio（使相等），源于 aequare（使平）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequare means to make equal or level.
items.cn: aequare 意为使相等、使平。

items.en: Aequatio names the act of making equal.
items.cn: aequatio 指使相等的动作。

items.en: Équation applies the word to algebra.
items.cn: 法语 équation 把这个词用于代数。

items.en: Modern English extends equation to chemistry and to mixed situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 equation 扩展到化学与复杂局面。

note.en: Equation is a balance word from the aequus family, close to formula and expression.
note.cn: equation 是来自 aequus 词族的「平衡」词，与 formula 和 expression 相邻。

entries.definition: to treat as equal
relating to an equation
the same in amount
a rule or relationship written in symbols
a group of mathematical symbols
an equation true for all values

normalIntro.en: Equation is a little balance: whatever is on one side of the equal sign must match the other.
normalIntro.cn: equation 是一架小天平：等号一边的东西必须与另一边相配。

normal.en: To solve an equation is to find the value that keeps both sides equal.
normal.cn: 解方程就是找出让两边保持相等的值。

normal.en: A linear equation draws a straight line on a graph.
normal.cn: 线性方程在图上画出一条直线。

normal.en: A chemical equation must be balanced atom by atom.
normal.cn: 化学方程式必须逐个原子配平。

normal.en: The other side of the equation means the factors you forgot.
normal.cn: 「the other side of the equation」指你忽略的另一面因素。

normal.en: Compare formula: a formula is a rule, an equation states equality.
normal.cn: 对比 formula：formula 是规则，equation 陈述相等关系。

abstract.en: Picture an equal sign holding two trays level.
abstract.cn: 想象一个等号托着两只水平的托盘。

abstract.en: Imagine atoms counted carefully on both sides of an arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象箭头两边被仔细数过的原子。

abstract.en: Think of a scale where cost sits on one pan and benefit on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一边是成本，一边是收益。

examples.en: She solved the equation in her head.
examples.cn: 她心算解出了这个方程。

examples.en: Every chemical equation must balance.
examples.cn: 每个化学方程式都必须配平。

examples.en: Time is the missing factor in the equation.
examples.cn: 时间是这一局面中缺失的因素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equ + ation」——把两边「弄成一样」，就是方程式；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequare（使相等）→ aequatio（使相等）→ 法语 équation → 英语 equation，核心义「两边相等的陈述」。

sensesIntro.en: Equation begins as a statement of mathematical equality, extends to chemistry, and then to any set of factors to balance.
sensesIntro.cn: equation 从数学上的相等陈述开始，扩展到化学，再扩展到任何需要权衡的因素组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides of an equal sign held in balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：等号两边保持平衡。

branches.en: The mathematical statement is the core sense.
branches.cn: 数学陈述是核心义项。

branches.en: Chemistry applies the equal-sign form to atoms.
branches.cn: 化学把等号形式用于原子。

branches.en: A real situation becomes sides that must be weighed.
branches.cn: 现实局面变成需要权衡的两边。

branches.en: Both a math equation and a hard choice involve balancing sides.
branches.cn: 数学方程与艰难选择都涉及平衡两边。

branches.en: Both math and chemistry equations must stay balanced.
branches.cn: 数学方程与化学方程式都必须保持平衡。

intro.en: Equation is a Latin noun of making equal, and English builds equate and equational around the same root.
intro.cn: equation 是拉丁语中表示「使相等」的名词，英语围绕同一词根构成 equate 与 equational。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, aequare means to make equal, and aequatio means a making equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequare 意为使相等，aequatio 意为使相等的过程。

definition_zh: 气泡；泡沫；冒泡
definition_en: a ball of air or gas inside a liquid
core_image: 肥皂泡在阳光下透出彩虹色
scene: 厨房里水壶刚刚烧开。 Soap bubbles rose from the warm water.
sceneCN: 这里 bubble 是「气泡」（第 1 个义项：液体中包着空气的小球）；句意是温水中升起一串肥皂泡。

senses.title: A ball of air in liquid
senses.definition: a small ball of air or gas inside a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 液体中包着空气或气体的小球
senses.example: Soap bubbles rose from the warm water.

definition_zh: 旅行者；旅客；游客；（吉卜赛）流浪者
definition_en: a person who is making a journey or who travels often
core_image: 一个人背着旧背包站在车站大钟下，手里攥着一张长途车票
scene: 长途车站的长椅上，一个背包客把车票与地图摊在膝上等夜车。 A tired traveller asked the way to the platform.
sceneCN: 这里 traveller 是「旅行者」（第 1 个义项：正在出行的人）；句意为一个疲惫的旅客问去站台怎么走。车站大钟下背旧包的人正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 名词：流浪民族成员（英式）

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -er 还原为动词，义为「旅行」
美式拼写，少一个 l，义同「旅行者」
由 travel 加 -ogue 构成，义为「旅行见闻录」

senses.title: A person on a journey
senses.definition: someone who is making a trip from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 正在从一处前往另一处的人
senses.example: The traveller arrived after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这位旅客午夜后才到。
senses.why: Travel came from an old word for labour, so a traveller is one who takes the trouble of a journey.
senses.whyCN: travel 来自表示「辛劳」的旧词，所以 traveller 就是经历过这趟辛苦的人。

senses.title: A person who travels often
senses.definition: someone who journeys frequently, for work or pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或游玩经常出行的人
senses.example: She is a seasoned traveller.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个走惯了路的人。
senses.why: Habit turns the name from a single trip into a description of a person.
senses.whyCN: 习惯使这个称呼从一趟行程变成对一个人的描述。

senses.title: A member of a travelling community
senses.definition: a member of a group, such as Irish Travellers, that moves about
senses.definitionCN: 如爱尔兰旅行者这类居无定所的群体成员
senses.example: The site is used by travellers in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这块场地夏天供流浪民族使用。
senses.why: The name takes a capital letter when it names a whole community rather than a single journey.
senses.whyCN: 当它命名一整个群体而非单次行程时，首字母要大写。

senses.title: A device that moves along something
senses.definition: a part, like a ring or pulley, that runs along a rail or rope
senses.definitionCN: 沿轨道或绳索移动的环、滑轮等部件
senses.example: A traveller runs along the overhead beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一个行件沿横梁滑动。
senses.why: The word for a person on the move is borrowed for a part that moves along a fixed line.
senses.whyCN: 用来指人的「在移动者」被借去指沿固定线路移动的零件。

senses.title: Someone who travels through time
senses.definition: a person imagined to move between different times
senses.definitionCN: 想象中在不同时间之间穿行的人
senses.example: The novel follows a time traveller.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说跟着一位时间旅行者。
senses.why: Time is treated as a country to be crossed, so the ordinary noun needs no new form.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成一个国家来穿越，所以这个普通名词不必换形。

intro.en: The word is travel plus -er, and travel itself comes from Old French travail, labour or hardship.
intro.cn: 这个词是 travel 加 -er，而 travel 本身来自古法语 travail（劳作、艰辛）。

items.en: Travail means labour, toil, or trouble, from a late Latin word for a torture device.
items.cn: 古法语 travail 意为劳作、辛苦，源自晚期拉丁语指刑具的词。

items.en: Travel still means hard going in Middle English, and the traveller is one who endures it.
items.cn: 中世纪英语里 travel 仍指艰苦的路途，traveller 就是承受它的人。

items.en: As journeys grow easier, the word loses its sting and simply means making a trip.
items.cn: 随着旅途变得容易，这个词失去苦味，只表示出行。

items.en: The -er ending marks the person, and American spelling drops one l.
items.cn: -er 词尾标记那个人，美式拼写少一个 l。

items.en: The capitalised form names travelling communities in Britain and Ireland.
items.cn: 首字母大写的形式在英伦指流浪民族群体。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on travel itself, while the near-meaning group names other people on the move.
note.cn: 形近组由 travel 本身构出，近义组列出其他在路上的人。

the act of making a journey

normalIntro.en: The -er ending does the work, once travel is known.
normalIntro.cn: 认识 travel 之后，-er 这个词尾就够用了。

normal.en: Travel is the verb, traveller is the person who does it.
normal.cn: travel 是动词，traveller 是干这件事的人。

normal.en: American English writes traveler with one l.
normal.cn: 美式英语写 traveler，只有一个 l。

normal.en: Traveller and trouble share an origin, in a word for toil.
normal.cn: traveller 与 trouble 同源，源头指辛劳。

normal.en: Fellow traveller means a companion on the way, or a political sympathiser.
normal.cn: fellow traveller 既指旅伴，也指政治上的同路人。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l before -er and -ing.
normal.cn: 英式拼写在 -er、-ing 前双写 l。

abstract.en: Picture one bag, one ticket, one clock above a wide station.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包、一张票、车站大钟。

abstract.en: Notice the bag is old and the shoes are dusty.
abstract.cn: 留意包很旧，鞋上有灰。

abstract.en: Then let the same figure step into another century.
abstract.cn: 再让同一个人跨进另一个世纪。

examples.en: The station was full of tired travellers.
examples.cn: 车站里挤满了疲惫的旅客。

examples.en: As a seasoned traveller, he packs in ten minutes.
examples.cn: 作为走惯路的人，他十分钟就收拾好行李。

examples.en: The museum tells the story of a time traveller.
examples.cn: 博物馆讲了一个时间旅行者的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿沃勒」——穿过一片沃野，勒紧背包的旅行者。

root: 古法语 travail（劳作、辛苦）+ 后缀 -er；同族有 travel、traveler、trouble

sensesIntro.en: The senses spread from one person on one journey to a whole community and to a moving machine part.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项从「一个人一趟行程」，扩展到一整个群体与一个会移动的零件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dusty backpacker waiting under a station clock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个满身灰尘的背包客在车站大钟下等车。

branches.en: The single-journey sense, the plainest use.
branches.cn: 单趟义：最朴素的用法。

branches.en: The habitual sense, where travel is a way of life.
branches.cn: 习惯义：旅行成了生活方式。

branches.en: The community sense, capitalised, tied to Britain and Ireland.
branches.cn: 群体义：首字母大写，与英伦相关。

branches.en: The mechanical sense, a part that runs along a beam.
branches.cn: 机械义：沿横梁滑动的部件。

branches.en: The imagined sense, crossing times rather than places.
branches.cn: 想象义：跨越的是时间而地点。

intro.en: The suffix marks the person, and travel has a French ancestor with a rough history.
intro.cn: 后缀标记人，而 travel 有个来历坎坷的法语祖先。

latinIntro.en: The stem travel- appears in travel, traveller, travelogue, and the American traveler.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 travel- 出现在 travel、traveller、travelogue 与美式 traveler 里。

items.meaning: the doubled l before the suffix
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写保留两个 l。

items.example: The American form drops one l.

items.meaning: a talk or book about travels

items.example: The trip was trouble from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这趟旅程从一开始就麻烦不断。

definition_zh: 谷物；谷粒；颗粒；一丝
definition_en: the seeds of grass plants used as food, a single seed, a tiny hard particle, or a small amount
core_image: 金黄的麦穗在风里低头，穗上每一粒都饱满紧实
scene: 农民把谷物装进麻袋。 The farmer poured grain into sacks.
sceneCN: 这里 grain 是「谷物」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民把谷物装进麻袋。

senses.title: Food from grass plants
senses.definition: the seeds of plants such as wheat and rice, used as food
senses.definitionCN: 小麦、水稻等植物的种子，用作食物
senses.example: The farmer poured grain into sacks.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把谷物装进麻袋。
senses.why: This is the agricultural sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的农业含义。

senses.title: A tiny particle
senses.definition: a single small hard piece of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物细小坚硬的一粒
senses.example: A grain of sand got into my shoe.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒沙子进了我的鞋里。
senses.why: Any small hard piece resembles a seed of wheat.
senses.whyCN: 任何细小坚硬的颗粒都像一粒麦子。

senses.title: A trace
senses.definition: a very small amount of a quality or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 某种品质或情感极小的分量
senses.example: There is a grain of truth in what he says.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话里有一点真实性。
senses.why: One seed is a tiny part of a harvest, as a trace is of a truth.
senses.whyCN: 一粒种子是收成的一小部分，正如一丝真实之于真相。

intro.en: Grain came from Latin granum, a seed, through French.
intro.cn: grain 从拉丁语 granum（种子）经法语而来。

items.en: Granum meant a seed or a small grain.
items.cn: granum 意为种子或谷粒。

items.en: Grain named grain and the seed of plants.
items.cn: grain 指谷物和植物的种子。

items.en: Grain entered English as the name of cereal crops.
items.cn: grain 以谷类作物的名称进入英语。

items.en: It spread to any small hard particle.
items.cn: 它扩展到任何细小的硬颗粒。

items.en: A grain of truth used the seed as a measure of amount.
items.cn: a grain of truth 用种子来度量分量。

note.en: Grain is compared with look-alike words and words for seeds.
note.cn: 把 grain 与形近词以及表示种子的词作比较。

entries.definition: large and impressive
of the colour of grass
to obtain
the part of a plant that grows a new plant
a grain used as food
the inner part of a seed

normalIntro.en: Grain begins as a seed and ends as a measure of anything small.
normalIntro.cn: grain 从一粒种子开始，最终成为衡量微小之物的尺度。

normal.en: The farmer poured grain into sacks.
normal.cn: 农民把谷物装进麻袋。

normal.en: A grain of sand got into my shoe.
normal.cn: 一粒沙子进了我的鞋里。

normal.en: There is a grain of truth in what he says.

normal.en: This bread is made from whole grain.

normal.en: He works against the grain of his nature.

abstract.en: One grain kept in the barn is worth a field in spring.
abstract.cn: 仓里留下一粒谷，春天就多一片田。

abstract.en: A grain of doubt can outweigh a mountain of proof.
abstract.cn: 一粒怀疑能压过一整座证据之山。

abstract.en: The smallest measure is still a measure.
abstract.cn: 最小的尺度仍然是尺度。

examples.en: There is a grain of truth in what he says.

dict_mnemonic.text: grain 源自拉丁语 granum（种子），指「谷物」，也指「颗粒」和「一丝」；a grain of sand 是「一粒沙」，whole grain 是「全谷物」，against the grain 是「违背本性」，grainy 是「有颗粒感的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 granum（种子、谷粒），经古法语 grain 进入英语，核心义为谷粒，引申为任何细小的硬颗粒以及极小的分量。

sensesIntro.en: Grain means cereal crops, a single small particle, or a very small amount.
sensesIntro.cn: grain 指谷类作物、单一的细小颗粒，或极小的分量。

core.en: A seed that can feed and can measure.
core.cn: 既能果腹又能计量的种子。

branches.en: Sacks of wheat fill the barn.
branches.cn: 一袋袋小麦堆满谷仓。

branches.en: One hard speck rolls around a shoe.
branches.cn: 一粒硬沙在鞋里滚动。

branches.en: A small truth hides inside a large claim.
branches.cn: 一个大说法里藏着一点真实。

branches.en: The crop and the single seed share one shape.
branches.cn: 作物与单粒种子共享一种形态。

branches.en: A sand grain and a grain of truth are both tiny units.
branches.cn: 一粒沙与一丝真实，都是微小的单位。

intro.en: Grain forms adjectives and nouns of seeds and stores.
intro.cn: grain 构成表示种子和储藏的形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is granum, a seed or grain.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 granum（种子、谷粒）。

The bag held a few grains of rice.
Each granule of salt is tiny.
The granary was full that year.

definition_zh: 嫉妒；羡慕；嫉妒的对象
definition_en: the feeling of wanting what someone else has, or to feel that way
core_image: 一个人盯着别人手里的果子，自己的手却空着
scene: 看到朋友的奖杯时，他心里生出一丝嫉妒。 A touch of envy rose in him when he saw his friend's trophy.
sceneCN: 这里 envy 是「嫉妒」（第 1 个义项：因别人拥有而心生不快或渴望）；句意：看到朋友的奖杯，他心里生出一丝嫉妒。

senses.title: The feeling of wanting another's good
senses.definition: an unhappy or longing feeling caused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck
senses.definitionCN: 因他人的财物、品质或运气而产生的不快或渴望
senses.example: Her success filled him with envy.
senses.exampleCN: 她的成功让他满心嫉妒。
senses.why: The Latin root means to look at someone with a grudging eye, which is exactly the feeling of envy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为带着不满的眼光看人，这正是嫉妒的感受。

senses.title: The person or thing envied
senses.definition: a person or thing that others wish they had
senses.definitionCN: 别人希望自己也能拥有的人或物
senses.example: Their garden is the envy of the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的花园让整条街的人羡慕。
senses.why: The feeling and its object share one word, so envy can name the admired thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 感受与对象共用一词，所以 envy 也可以指被羡慕的事物本身。

senses.title: To feel envy toward someone
senses.definition: to feel unhappy longing because another person has something
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有某物而感到不快而渴望
senses.example: He envied his brother's easy confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他嫉妒哥哥那份从容的自信。
senses.why: The verb turns the feeling into an action directed at a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词形式把这股感受变成指向某人的动作。

intro.en: Envy comes from Latin invidia, from invidere, to look upon with malice, built on in-, against, and videre, to see.
intro.cn: envy 来自拉丁语 invidia，源自动词 invidere（带着恶意看），由 in-（对着）与 videre（看）构成。

items.en: Videre means to see.
items.cn: videre 意为看见。

items.en: Invidere means to look at with a hostile eye.
items.cn: invidere 意为带着敌意看。

items.en: Invidia names the feeling of envy.
items.cn: invidia 指嫉妒这种感受。

items.en: Envie carries the word into French.
items.cn: envie 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Envy appears in English with the same hostile longing.
items.cn: 中古英语 envy 带着同样的敌意渴望出现。

items.en: Modern English also uses envy for a milder wish to have something.
items.cn: 现代英语也用 envy 表示较温和的「希望拥有」。

note.en: Envy is a seeing-rooted feeling word, close to its envious family and to jealousy.
note.cn: envy 是一个源于「看」的感受词，与 envious 词族以及 jealousy 相邻。

entries.definition: feeling envy
with envy
likely to cause envy or offense
fear of losing what one has to a rival
to want something belonging to another
to feel unhappy about another's good fortune

normalIntro.en: Envy comes from looking: the envious eye keeps watching what someone else holds.
normalIntro.cn: envy 来自「看」：嫉妒的眼睛总盯着别人手里的东西。

normal.en: Green with envy is a common phrase for strong jealousy.
normal.cn: green with envy 是表示强烈嫉妒的常用短语。

normal.en: The envy of the street means the thing everyone wants.
normal.cn: the envy of the street 指人人想要的东西。

normal.en: Envious is the adjective, as in an envious glance.
normal.cn: envious 是形容词，如 an envious glance。

normal.en: Envy can be a noun or a verb without changing shape.
normal.cn: envy 可作名词也可作动词，词形不变。

normal.en: Compare jealousy: jealousy fears loss, envy wants another's good.
normal.cn: 对比 jealousy：jealousy 害怕失去，envy 渴望别人的好。

abstract.en: Picture an eye fixed on a fruit in another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛盯着别人手中的果子。

abstract.en: Imagine a green shadow falling over a smiling face.
abstract.cn: 想象一层绿色阴影落在一张笑脸上。

abstract.en: Think of a locked gate with a crowd gazing through.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门，一群人往里张望。

examples.en: He spoke of her promotion with open envy.
examples.cn: 他谈起她升职时毫不掩饰地流露出嫉妒。

examples.en: The little café is the envy of the neighborhood.
examples.cn: 这家小咖啡馆让整个街区羡慕。

examples.en: I envy her calm manner under pressure.
examples.cn: 我羡慕她在压力下的从容。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + vy」——看到别人的好就「眼红」，眼睛发绿；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（对着）＋ videre（看）→ invidere（带恶意地看）→ invidia（嫉妒）→ 古法语 envie → 英语 envy，核心义「看着别人的好而心生渴望」。

sensesIntro.en: Envy names the feeling, then the admired object, and finally the verb of feeling it toward someone.
sensesIntro.cn: envy 先指嫉妒的感受，再指被羡慕的对象，最后指对某人产生这种感受的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed gaze on something held by another.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光牢牢盯着别人手中的东西。

branches.en: The longing feeling is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 渴望的感受是核心名词义项。

branches.en: The admired object is called the envy of others.
branches.cn: 被羡慕的对象被称为他人的 envy。

branches.en: The verb directs the feeling at a person.
branches.cn: 动词把这种感受指向某人。

branches.en: A thing becomes the envy of others because it stirs the feeling.
branches.cn: 某物之所以成为他人羡慕的对象，是因为它激起了这种感受。

branches.en: To envy someone is to carry the noun feeling into action.
branches.cn: 嫉妒某人，就是把名词的感受化为行动。

intro.en: Envy is a Latin seeing word, with English relatives envious and enviously and the same-root invidious.
intro.cn: envy 是拉丁语中与「看」有关的词，英语亲属有 envious、enviously 以及同根的 invidious。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre means to see, and invidere means to look at with ill will.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看见，invidere 意为带着恶意看。

items.example: In- directs the look against someone.

items.exampleCN: invidere 把看与敌意结合起来。

items.example: Envie carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: envie 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Envy keeps both noun and verb uses.
items.exampleCN: envy 同时保留名词与动词用法。
enviously 描述某人看的方式。

definition_zh: 加强的；集中的；密集的；精耕细作的
definition_en: involving a lot of effort, work, or attention in a short period, or concentrated on one area
core_image: 一小块地里插满了苗，水和肥料都浇到同几垄上
scene: 教室里只有六个人，两周内每天八节课，教材翻到了最后几页。 The hospital opened a new intensive care unit on the top floor.
sceneCN: 这里 intensive 是「加强的、密集的」（第 1 个义项：短期投入大量精力），句意医院在顶层新开了重症监护病房，即集中照护的地方。画面里的物件：教材、病区指示牌、护理记录。

pos.zh: 形容词：加强的；集中的；密集的；精耕细作的

derivatives.zh: 由同一词干构成，义为「强度」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「密集地」
由同一词干加 -ify 构成，义为「加强」
由同一词干构成，义为「强烈的」

senses.title: Concentrated in time
senses.definition: involving much effort and attention in a short period
senses.definitionCN: 在短期内投入大量精力与注意力
senses.example: The students took an intensive course in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在夏天上了一个强化课程。
senses.why: The suffix -ive means "tending to", so intensive describes effort gathered onto one point.
senses.whyCN: -ive 意为「倾向于」，因此 intensive 形容力量聚于一点。

senses.title: Of land and farming
senses.definition: using a lot of labour, water, and fertilizer on a small area of land
senses.definitionCN: 在小面积土地上投入大量人工、水与肥料
senses.example: Intensive farming feeds more people from fewer fields.
senses.exampleCN: 集约农业用更少的田地养活更多的人。
senses.why: Agriculture borrowed the idea of effort concentrated on one plot.
senses.whyCN: 农业借用了「精力集中于一小块地」这一想法。

senses.title: Of medical care
senses.definition: giving constant close attention to a seriously ill patient
senses.definitionCN: 对危重病人给予持续的密切照护
senses.example: She spent a week in intensive care after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故后她在重症监护病房住了一周。
senses.why: Hospitals needed a word for care with no moment left unattended.
senses.whyCN: 医院需要一个词来形容每一刻都不放空的照护。

senses.title: Grammar: adding force
senses.definition: added to a word to strengthen it, as very does
senses.definitionCN: 加在词上以加强语气，如 very 的作用
senses.example: The adverb is used here as an intensive word.
senses.exampleCN: 这里这个副词起了强调作用。
senses.why: Grammarians applied the same metaphor to words that press harder.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家把同一比喻用到了「加力」的词上。

intro.en: Intensive adds the Latin ending -ivus "tending to" to the participle of intendere.
intro.cn: intensive 在 intendere 的分词上加拉丁词尾 -ivus「倾向于」。

items.en: Tendere "to stretch" with in- gives intendere, to strain towards something.
items.cn: tendere「伸展」加 in- 构成 intendere「向某物绷紧」。

items.en: Intensus was the past participle, used of a drawn bow or attentive mind.
items.cn: intensus 是过去分词，用于拉开的弓或专注的心。

items.en: The ending -ivus marked a tendency or direction of action.
items.cn: 词尾 -ivus 标出动作的倾向或方向。

items.en: English formed intensive in the seventeenth century for effort gathered in one place.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪造出 intensive，指力量集于一处。

items.en: Farming, medicine, and language teaching each adopted it in turn.
items.cn: 农业、医学与语言教学先后各自采用了它。

note.en: The look-alike group differs from intense only by the ending; the near-meaning group holds words for concentrated effort.
note.cn: 形近组与 intense 只差词尾；近义组收表示集中投入的词。

entries.definition: Very strong in degree, of heat or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指程度强烈，多用于热或感受。

entries.definition: The measured strength of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为可测量的强度。

entries.definition: Covering a wide area rather than a deep point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广泛的」，铺开而非集中。

entries.definition: Complete in every part, with nothing skipped.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「彻底的」，没有遗漏。

entries.definition: Gathered into one place or brought to full strength.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「集中的」，汇于一处或加大浓度。

entries.definition: Strict and demanding in standards.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「严格的」，要求高。

normalIntro.en: The hooks lean on the difference between intensive and intense and on real course names.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 intensive 与 intense 的差别，也借助真实的课程名称。

normal.en: Intensive work is piled into days; intense work merely feels extreme.
normal.cn: intensive 是几天里塞满活儿，intense 只是感觉极端。

normal.en: An intensive course trades length for density.
normal.cn: 强化课程用短时间换高密度。

normal.en: Intensive care watches every breath.
normal.cn: 重症监护盯着每一次呼吸。

normal.en: Intensive farming squeezes more from one field.
normal.cn: 集约农业从一块地里挤出更多产出。

normal.en: Intensive reading takes ten pages slowly.
normal.cn: 精读就是很慢地读十页。

abstract.en: Intensive means one spot held under a burning glass.
abstract.cn: 密集就是以燃烧的透镜照住一处。

abstract.en: Not wider, only deeper: that is the intensive way.
abstract.cn: 不求更宽，只求更深，这就是密集的路子。

abstract.en: Some learning must be pressed, like coffee.
abstract.cn: 有些学习必须像咖啡一样被压实。

examples.en: He signed up for a four-week intensive German course.
examples.cn: 他报了一个四周的德语强化课程。

examples.en: Intensive training left the team strong but tired.
examples.cn: 密集训练让队伍变强，也很疲惫。

examples.en: The farmer turned his small plot into intensive rice fields.
examples.cn: 这位农民把小地块改成了精耕稻田。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因太细五」——学习细到五个点都抠，就是强化

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」→ intensus「拉紧的」+ -ivus「倾向于」→ 英语 intensive。同族：intense、intensity、intensify。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: short concentrated effort, farming, medical care, and grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：短期集中投入、农业经营、医疗照护，以及语法上的强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small plot crowded with seedlings and watched every day.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块地里插满苗，天天有人看顾。

branches.en: THE SUMMER COURSE: hours are packed into weeks.
branches.cn: 暑期课程这条线：课时塞进几周里。

branches.en: THE SMALL FIELD: land is worked hard, not widely.
branches.cn: 小田块这条线：地是精耕的，不是铺开的。

branches.en: THE WARD: attention never lets go of the patient.
branches.cn: 病房这条线：注意力一刻不离病人。

branches.en: THE STRESS WORD: a little very presses the meaning harder.
branches.cn: 强调词这条线：一个小小的 very 把意思压得更重。

branches.en: THE LINK: both spend attention in a narrow, constant way.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把注意力窄而持续地投下去。

intro.en: Intensive = in- "towards" + tens- "stretch" + -ive "tending to".
intro.cn: intensive = in-「朝向」+ tens-「伸展」+ -ive「倾向于」。

latinIntro.en: Latin intensus and the ending -ivus are both attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intensus 与词尾 -ivus 均有记载。

definition_zh: 药店；兼售日用品的药房；（英国）药房
definition_en: a shop that sells medicines and also many everyday goods, or the pharmacy counter inside a larger store
core_image: 街角一家亮着灯的小店，药盒与洗发水并排摆在架上
scene: 街角的小店门口挂着营业到午夜的牌子，玻璃门里透着暖光。 She ran into the drugstore to buy cough syrup.
sceneCN: 这里 drugstore 是「兼售日用品的药房」（第 1 个义项：出售药品与日常用品的商店）；句意是她跑进那家药房去买止咳糖浆。

pos.zh: 名词：药店；兼售日用品的药房

collocations.zh: 药房出售的平价化妆品

derivatives.zh: 由 drug 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「药剂师；药商」
构成 drugstore 的核心语素，义为「药物；毒品」

senses.title: A shop selling medicines and everyday goods
senses.definition: a shop, especially in North America, that sells medicines, toiletries and many household goods
senses.definitionCN: 尤指北美的商店，出售药品、洗漱用品和许多日用杂货
senses.example: She picked up her prescription at the drugstore.
senses.exampleCN: 她在药房取了处方药。
senses.why: American drugstores grew into general shops because a small town needed one counter for medicine and everything else at once.
senses.whyCN: 美式药房之所以发展成杂货店，是因为小镇需要一个柜台同时解决药品和其余所有日常所需。

senses.title: The pharmacy counter
senses.definition: the section inside a larger shop where prescriptions are filled and medicines are sold
senses.definitionCN: 较大商店内部负责配处方、出售药品的区域
senses.example: The drugstore counter is at the back of the supermarket.
senses.exampleCN: 药房柜台在超市的后面。
senses.why: The same word can name the counter rather than the building, because the counter is where the medical function actually happens.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也可以指柜台而非整家店，因为真正承担医疗功能的正是那个柜台。

senses.title: The British equivalent
senses.definition: used in British English for a chemist's shop, where medicines are dispensed
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中指 chemist's shop，即配发药品的药店
senses.example: In Britain the same kind of shop is usually called a chemist, not a drugstore.
senses.exampleCN: 在英国，同类商店通常叫 chemist，而不叫 drugstore。
senses.why: British usage prefers chemist for the dispensing shop, so drugstore works there mainly as an American import or a sign of difference.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语更常用 chemist 来指配药的商店，所以 drugstore 在那里主要是个美式借词或差异标志。

intro.en: Drugstore is a transparent American compound of drug and store, named for what the shop sold before it became a general store.
intro.cn: drugstore 是透明的美式复合词，由 drug 与 store 组成，命名依据是这家店在变成杂货店之前所卖的东西。

items.en: Old French drogue meant a medicine or a pharmacy material, and it supplied the English word drug.
items.cn: 古法语 drogue 意为「药物」或药房原料，是英语 drug 的来源。

items.en: English drug is recorded from the fourteenth century, first in medical and trade texts.
items.cn: 英语 drug 自十四世纪有记录，最早见于医学与贸易文本。

items.en: A druggist was the person who prepared and sold drugs, so the shop was first called the druggist's.
items.cn: druggist 指配制和出售药物的人，因此这家店最初被叫作 druggist's。

items.en: In nineteenth-century America, drug store named the shop itself, and the two words were often written apart.
items.cn: 在十九世纪的美国，drug store 直接指这家店，两个词常分开书写。

items.en: The compound drugstore settled into one word as these shops added toiletries, snacks and household goods.
items.cn: 随着这类商店增加洗漱用品、零食和日用品，复合词 drugstore 逐渐连写成一个词。

items.en: The word now also names the pharmacy counter inside a supermarket and is contrasted with the British chemist.
items.cn: 这个词如今也指超市里的药房柜台，并与英式的 chemist 形成对照。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the building blocks and a near-spelling relative; the near-meaning group compares the shop names used in different countries.
note.cn: 形近组收构成这个词的部件和一个拼写相近的亲属词；近义组比较不同国家使用的店名。

entries.definition: The substance a drugstore sells; the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指药房出售的药物，是这一复合词的第一个成分。

entries.definition: A person who prepares and sells medicines; the older name behind the shop.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指配制和出售药品的人，是这家店更早的命名依据。

entries.definition: A shop or a supply kept for use; the second element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商店、储备」，是这一复合词的第二个成分。

entries.definition: An old American slang term for a young man who idles around drugstores.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，美国旧时俚语，指在药房里闲荡的年轻人。

entries.definition: A shop or department where medicines are prepared and sold; more formal and more strictly medical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「药房、药店」，更正式，医学色彩更强。

entries.definition: The British name for a shop that dispenses medicines; also a scientist in chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语指配药的药房，也可指化学家。

entries.definition: A small shop open long hours selling food and everyday items, often without a pharmacy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指营业时间长、出售食品和日用品的小店，通常没有药房。

entries.definition: An old word for a person or shop that prepared and sold medicines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，旧时指配制和出售药物的人或店铺。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the compound into its two real parts and then follow the shop from pharmacy to general store.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把这个复合词拆成真实的两部分，再跟着这家店从药房走到杂货店。

normal.en: Drugstore is drug plus store: literally a store for drugs.
normal.cn: drugstore 就是 drug 加 store，字面意思是「卖药的店」。

normal.en: In America the shop grew beyond medicine, so shelves now hold shampoo, snacks and batteries too.
normal.cn: 在美国，这类店超出了药品范围，所以货架上如今也摆着洗发水、零食和电池。

normal.en: A druggist is the person; a drugstore is the place; the -ist and the store tell them apart.
normal.cn: druggist 是人，drugstore 是地方；-ist 和 store 把两者区分开。

normal.en: In Britain, say chemist for the same kind of shop.
normal.cn: 在英国，同类商店要说 chemist。

normal.en: The drugstore counter is the medical part inside a larger shop.
normal.cn: drugstore counter 是较大商店里承担医疗功能的那一部分。

abstract.en: Picture one lit window at a street corner, with a shelf that holds both pills and toothpaste.
abstract.cn: 想象街角一扇亮着的窗，架子上既摆着药片也摆着牙膏。

abstract.en: The same shop is drawn twice: once as a clinic counter, once as a neighbourhood general store.
abstract.cn: 同一家店被画了两次：一次是诊所式柜台，一次是社区杂货铺。

abstract.en: Drugstore is a word about convenience: health and daily life sold at the same counter.
abstract.cn: drugstore 是一个关于便利的词：健康与日常生活摆在同一张柜台上出售。

examples.en: She picked up her prescription at the drugstore.
examples.cn: 她在药房取了处方药。

examples.en: The drugstore on the corner stays open until midnight.
examples.cn: 街角那家药房营业到午夜。

examples.en: He bought shampoo and batteries at the drugstore.
examples.cn: 他在药房买了洗发水和电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: drug 是「药」，store 是「商店」，合起来就是「卖药的商店」，美式英语里它兼卖日用品。

root: 由 drug「药物」与 store「商店」复合而成；drug 经由古法语 drogue 进入英语，更早来源不确定。十九世纪美国用 drug store 指这类商店，后连写为 drugstore。store 经由古法语 estore 来自拉丁语 instaurare「恢复、置办」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of drugstore move from the American general shop to its pharmacy counter and finally to the British shop it is compared with.
sensesIntro.cn: drugstore 的三个义项从美式杂货药房，移到店内的药房柜台，最后落到与它相对的英式药房。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit corner shop where pills and shampoo share one shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一家亮着灯的街角小店，药片与洗发水共用一层货架。

branches.en: THE AMERICAN SHOP: medicine is the reason for the shop, and everyday goods fill the rest of it.
branches.cn: 美式商店线：药品是开店的理由，日用品填满了其余空间。

branches.en: THE COUNTER: inside a bigger shop, the pharmacy desk keeps the medical core.
branches.cn: 柜台线：在更大的商店里，药房柜台保留了医疗核心。

branches.en: THE BRITISH TWIN: the same kind of shop carries a different name across the Atlantic.
branches.cn: 英式双生线：同类商店跨过大西洋换了一个名字。

branches.en: TWO NAMES, ONE ROLE: drugstore and chemist both sell and dispense medicines.
branches.cn: 两名一职：drugstore 与 chemist 都出售并配发药品。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL CORE: the counter and the dispensing shop are where the health function really lives.
branches.cn: 医疗核心：柜台与配药商店才是健康功能真正所在。

intro.en: Drugstore is a two-part English compound; each part has its own history, and only the second has a Latin past.
intro.cn: drugstore 是两部分组成的英语复合词；两部分各有来历，只有第二部分有拉丁语渊源。

latinIntro.en: Store goes back through Old French to Latin instaurare, to restore or set up; drug has no settled Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: store 经由古法语可追溯到拉丁语 instaurare（恢复、置办）；drug 则没有确立的拉丁语祖先。

items.example: The first element supplies the medical purpose.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分提供医学用途。

items.meaning: a place where goods are kept and sold
items.meaningCN: 存放并出售货物的地方
items.example: The second element supplies the retail setting.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供零售场景。

items.meaning: a long table for serving customers
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 drugstore counter 中。

items.meaning: a group of shops under one company
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 drugstore chain 中。

items.meaning: a young man who idles in drugstores
items.meaningCN: 在药房里闲荡的年轻人
items.example: The idiom is old American slang.
items.exampleCN: 这个习语是美国旧时俚语。

items.meaning: inexpensive cosmetics sold in such shops
items.meaningCN: 此类商店出售的平价化妆品
items.example: The phrase marks the everyday-goods side of the shop.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语标出了这家店的日用品一面。

derivatives.zh: 由 drug 加表人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「药剂师；药商」
构成 drugstore 的核心语素，义为「药物；毒品」

definition_zh: 宽度；广度；宽度单位；宽容
definition_en: the measurement of something from one side to the other, and by extension the breadth of a range
core_image: 一把卷尺横拉过门框，尺上的数字正好停在九十几厘米
scene: 木匠把卷尺横着拉过门框，报出那一串数字，说这扇门就按这个宽度做。 Measure the width of the window before you order the curtains.
sceneCN: 这里 width 是「宽度」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边量出的尺寸）；句意为订窗帘前先量出窗户的宽度。卷尺横拉过门框、数字停在那一格，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The measurement across
senses.definition: the distance a thing measures from one side to the other, the smaller of its two flat dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 物体从一边到另一边量出的距离，平面上两个尺寸中较小的那个
senses.example: Measure the width of the window before you order the curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 订窗帘前先量出窗户的宽度。
senses.why: The noun takes the adjective and turns the quality into a number you can write down.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把形容词的性质变成了能写下来的数字。

senses.title: A stated measure
senses.definition: used after a number to give the measurement, as in a width of three metres
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字之后给出尺寸，如 a width of three metres
senses.example: The table has a width of one metre and a half.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子宽一米半。
senses.why: The same word doubles as a unit, since English says a width of rather than a wide of.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词又充当量词，因为英语说 a width of，而不说 a wide of。

senses.title: Breadth of a range
senses.definition: the extent or variety included in something, especially knowledge or choice
senses.definitionCN: 某物所包含的程度或多样程度，尤指知识或选择
senses.example: The width of her reading surprised the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 她阅读面的广博让全班都很惊讶。
senses.why: A physical span became a mental one, and the measurement now counts kinds instead of metres.
senses.whyCN: 物理的跨度变成心智的跨度，度量的对象也从米变成种类。

senses.title: In textile and cut sizes
senses.definition: the measurement of cloth from selvedge to selvedge, as sold in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 商店出售布料时从一边布边到另一边的尺寸
senses.example: This cloth comes in two widths, ninety and one hundred and fifty centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这种布有九十厘米和一百五十厘米两种幅宽。
senses.why: Shops need a fixed measure of cloth, so the general word became a trade term.
senses.whyCN: 商店需要固定的布料尺寸，于是普通词成了行业术语。

senses.title: In swimming pools and boats
senses.definition: used in the name of a pool or a boat class to state how wide it is
senses.definitionCN: 在泳池或船级名称中说明其宽度
senses.example: The pool has six lanes and a width of twenty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泳池有六条泳道，宽二十米。
senses.why: A standard measure became part of a name, and swimmers now speak of a twenty-metre width.
senses.whyCN: 一种标准度量进入了名称，游泳者于是说起「二十米宽」这样的说法。

intro.en: Width was formed in Middle English by adding the ending -th to wid, the same way length came from long and depth from deep.
intro.cn: width 是中古英语在 wid 上加词尾 -th 构成的，正如 length 来自 long、depth 来自 deep。

items.en: The adjective wid meant broad, and the ending -th already built nouns of measure such as lengu.
items.cn: 形容词 wid 表示宽阔，词尾 -th 早已能构成度量名词。

items.en: Widthe appeared as the noun of measurement, modelled on length and breadth.
items.cn: widthe 作为度量名词出现，仿照 length 与 breadth 的模式。

items.en: The spelling settled as width, with the short i of wide but a different vowel in careful speech.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 width，在某些口音里元音与 wide 略有不同。

items.en: Trade and tailoring gave it concrete uses such as the width of cloth.
items.cn: 商业与裁缝给了它具体用法，如布料的幅宽。

items.en: It also took an abstract life, so a person can have width of experience.
items.cn: 它也获得了抽象的生命，于是人可以有阅历之广度。

note.en: The first group gathers the other measurements of the same shape, the second the words that stand for breadth.
note.cn: 第一组收同一形状的其他度量名词，第二组收表示广度的词。

entries.definition: The measurement end to end, from long.
The measurement down, from deep.
The measurement across, from broad.
A preposition that merely looks close.
The same idea, often in a literary tone.
The full reach from one end to the other.
The extent covered by a set of things.

normalIntro.en: Width belongs to the th-family: length, depth, breadth, width, all nouns of measurement.
normalIntro.cn: width 属于 -th 家族：length、depth、breadth、width，都是度量名词。

normal.en: Long makes length and wide makes width, the -th is the measuring tool.
normal.cn: long 变 length，wide 变 width，那个 -th 就是量尺。

normal.en: Length runs along, width runs across, depth runs down.
normal.cn: length 竖着走，width 横着走，depth 往下走。

normal.en: A width of two metres never says a wide of two metres.
normal.cn: 要说 a width of two metres，不能说 a wide of。

normal.en: Width of reading counts kinds, not metres.
normal.cn: width of reading 数的是种类，不是米。

normal.en: Width and depth together describe a swimming pool.
normal.cn: width 与 depth 合起来描述一个泳池。

abstract.en: Feel a tape pulled tight across a door frame.
abstract.cn: 感觉卷尺绷紧横过门框。

abstract.en: See a number written down and the measure fixed for good.
abstract.cn: 看见数字被写下来，尺寸就此固定。

abstract.en: Hear cloth measured from edge to edge on a counter.
abstract.cn: 听柜台上的布从一边量到另一边。

examples.en: The width of the path is only one metre.
examples.cn: 这条小路的宽度只有一米。

examples.en: The skirt is available in three widths.
examples.cn: 这条裙子有三种宽度可选。

examples.en: What she lacks in width she makes up for in detail.
examples.cn: 她在广度上不足，便用细节来补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微斯」——微微一点宽度也要量出来。

root: 古英语 wid（宽阔）+ 度量名词词尾 -th → 中古英语 widthe → 现代英语 width；同族有 wide、widen、widely、length、depth。

sensesIntro.en: The noun fixes the distance across, doubles as a unit, widens into mental breadth, and settles into the trades of cloth and pools.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词固定了横量的距离，兼作量词，扩展到心智的广度，并固定于布料与泳池行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure stretched across a door frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷绷紧横过门框的卷尺。

branches.en: The curtain branch: measuring before ordering.
branches.cn: 窗帘分支：下订之前先量。

branches.en: The table branch: a width of one and a half metres.
branches.cn: 桌子分支：宽一米半。

branches.en: The reading branch: a class surprised by breadth.
branches.cn: 阅读分支：让全班惊讶的阅读广度。

branches.en: The trade branch: cloth in two widths.
branches.cn: 行业分支：两种幅宽的布料。

branches.en: The pool branch: six lanes, twenty metres wide.
branches.cn: 泳池分支：六条泳道，宽二十米。

intro.en: Width is a noun of quality and measure built with -th on an adjective, one of a small and ancient pattern.
intro.cn: width 是用 -th 加在形容词上构成的度量类抽象名词，属于一个小而古老的模式。

latinIntro.en: The base is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show the borrowed nouns of the same kind.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示同类的借入名词。

items.example: It forms width, length and depth.
A fixed frame after a number.
A common unit in sport and clothing.
items.exampleCN: 运动与服装中常见的度量。

definition_zh: 工人；工作者；雇员；工蜂；工蚁
definition_en: a person who does work, especially one employed in a job, or an insect such as a bee that does the work of the group
core_image: 清晨厂房门口一排安全帽，每个人的手上都有旧伤
scene: 厂门口的打卡机前，几个人一边排队一边咬着还没吃完的早点。 The workers asked for safer machines after the accident last month.
sceneCN: 这里 worker 是「工人、雇员」（第 1 个义项：受雇做事的人）；句意为工人们要求在上个月的事故之后更换更安全的机器。清晨厂门口一排安全帽，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 工蜂；工蚁（群体中负责劳作的个体）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -er 得到的动词，义为「工作；运转」
由 work 与 force 复合，义为「劳动力；全体员工」
由 worker 与 owned 复合，义为「工人所有的」

senses.title: The person who labours
senses.definition: a person who works, especially one who does physical or paid work
senses.definitionCN: 做事的人，尤指从事体力或受薪工作的人
senses.example: The workers asked for safer machines after the accident last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的事故之后，工人们要求换成更安全的机器。
senses.why: The ending -er means the one who does, so the verb for labour becomes the name of a person.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 表示「做某事的人」，于是劳作的动词变成了人的称呼。

senses.title: The office employee
senses.definition: a person employed in an office, a service or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室、服务行业或专业领域受雇的人
senses.example: She is an office worker who commutes two hours each way.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个上班族，单程要通勤两个小时。
senses.why: The same doer ending works indoors too, so a desk job keeps the name of labour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示行事者的词尾在室内也照样能用，于是坐办公桌的活仍带着「劳作」的名字。

senses.title: The insect that labours
senses.definition: a member of a bee or ant colony that does the collecting and building work
senses.definitionCN: 蜂群或蚁群中负责采集与建造的个体
senses.example: The workers of the hive carried pollen all day while the queen stayed inside.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂箱里的工蜂整天搬运花粉，蜂王留在里面。
senses.why: The name of a working person stretches to the insects whose whole life is work for the group.
senses.whyCN: 「劳作的人」这一称呼，延伸到一生都为群体劳作的昆虫身上。

intro.en: Worker is the Old English verb weorc plus the ending -er, which names the person who does the action.
intro.cn: worker 是古英语动词 weorc 加词尾 -er，用来称呼做这个动作的人。

items.en: The verb form was wyrcan, to do or to make, and the ending -ere named the doer.
items.cn: 动词形式是 wyrcan（做、造），词尾 -ere 指做事的人。

items.en: The ending weakened to -er, and the word settled as worker.
items.cn: 词尾弱化为 -er，这个词固定为 worker。

items.en: With the growth of factories the word became the everyday name of the employed.
items.cn: 随着工厂兴起，这个词成了受雇者的日常称呼。

items.en: The compound workforce appeared to name all the workers of a place together.
items.cn: 复合词 workforce 出现，用来统称一个地方的全部工人。

items.en: Natural history borrowed the word for the labouring members of a bee or ant colony.
items.cn: 博物学借这个词来指蜂群或蚁群中劳作的个体。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem in other shapes, the second holds other names for people who labour.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他形态，第二组收其他称呼劳动者的词。

entries.definition: To labour, or the job itself.
More than one worker.
All the people who work in a place.
A person who does hard physical work.
A person hired to work for another.
All the people who work for an organisation.

normalIntro.en: Worker is work plus -er, the plainest pattern in English for turning an action into a person.
normalIntro.cn: worker 是 work 加 -er，是英语里把动作变成人的最朴素做法。

normal.en: The ending -er says the one who does, as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 表示做某事的人，如 teacher 与 builder。

normal.en: Work plus er keeps every letter: worker, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: work 加 er 时每个字母都保留：worker，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Factory worker and office worker show the word needs a place to be exact.
normal.cn: factory worker 与 office worker 说明这个词需要地点来限定。

normal.en: A hard worker is not a strong worker: one praises effort, the other strength.
normal.cn: a hard worker 不等于 a strong worker：一个夸努力，一个说力气。

normal.en: The plural workers is also used for the whole class of employed people.
normal.cn: 复数 workers 也用来指整个受雇阶层。

abstract.en: A row of hard hats at the gate in early light.
abstract.cn: 晨光里门口一排安全帽。

abstract.en: A badge worn thin at one corner.
abstract.cn: 一枚一角磨薄的工牌。

abstract.en: Hands that know a tool better than a face.
abstract.cn: 一双手比一张脸更认得工具。

examples.en: The workers stopped for lunch at noon and sat on the steps.
examples.cn: 中午工人们停工吃饭，坐在台阶上。

examples.en: She is a careful worker who checks every page twice.
examples.cn: 她做事仔细，每一页都核对两遍。

examples.en: The workers in the hive never seem to rest.
examples.cn: 蜂巢里的工蜂好像从不休息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我克」加 -er：一个个难关都「克」过来的人，就是工人。

root: 古英语 wyrcan（做、造）+ 施事词尾 -ere → worker；与 work 同根，词族含 workforce、working。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the strong person who labours, widens to anyone employed, and then stretches to the insects that work for the colony.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从出力劳动的人开始，扩展到一切受雇者，再延伸到为群体劳作的昆虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of hard hats at the factory gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：厂门口一排安全帽。

branches.en: The factory branch: workers asking for safer machines.
branches.cn: 工厂分支：要求更安全机器的工人。

branches.en: The office branch: a commuter two hours from home.
branches.cn: 办公室分支：通勤两小时的职员。

branches.en: The insect branch: bees carrying pollen all day.
branches.cn: 昆虫分支：整日搬运花粉的工蜂。

branches.en: The class branch: workers as a group with shared demands.
branches.cn: 阶层分支：作为群体的工人。

branches.en: The effort branch: the one who does the work of the whole.
branches.cn: 劳作分支：承担整个群体活儿的那一个。

intro.en: Worker is the simplest kind of derivative in English: a verb stem plus the agent ending -er.
intro.cn: worker 是英语里最简单的一种派生：动词词干加施事词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but the agent ending has a Latin counterpart in -or, as in labourer's cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，但施事词尾在拉丁语里对应 -or。

items.exampleCN: 它由 work 构成 worker。
它与 worker 并存为 working。

items.example: An older way to say the same.
The old word marked the sex.

definition_zh: 处理掉；使倾向于
definition_en: to get rid of something, or to make someone likely to feel or act in a certain way
core_image: 一个人把旧箱子搬到门口，回头看了一眼空出来的角落
scene: 旧箱子被搬到门口，他回头看了一眼空出来的角落。 They disposed of the old files before moving.
sceneCN: 这里 dispose 指「处理掉」（第 1 个义项：把不要的东西清走）；句意是搬家前他们把旧文件处理掉了。

senses.title: To get rid of something
senses.definition: to throw away or deal with something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 把不要的东西扔掉或处置掉
senses.example: They disposed of the old files.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧文件处理掉了。
senses.why: A cleared corner is the first sign of a move.
senses.whyCN: 空出来的角落，是搬家的第一个信号。

senses.title: To make someone inclined
senses.definition: to make someone likely to feel or act in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 使某人倾向于某种感受或行动
senses.example: The warm welcome disposed her to stay.
senses.exampleCN: 热情的欢迎使她愿意留下。
senses.why: A room can lean a mind before a word is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 屋子在开口之前，就能让心思偏过去。

intro.en: Dispose comes from Latin disponere, to set out in order, from dis- and ponere, to place.
intro.cn: dispose 来自拉丁语 disponere（分置、安排），由 dis- 与 ponere（放置）构成。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or put down.
items.cn: ponere 指放置、放下。

items.en: Disponere meant to set each thing in its own place.
items.cn: disponere 指把每样东西各摆其位。

items.en: Disposer meant to arrange or to settle.
items.cn: 古法语 disposer 指安排或了结。

items.en: English dispose added the sense of getting rid of.
items.cn: 英语 dispose 添上处理掉的意思。

items.en: The word now also leans a mind toward a choice.
items.cn: 今天它也指让心思偏向某个选择。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dispose stem, and the meaning group names other ways of clearing or leaning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dispose 词干，近义组列出别的清理与倾斜说法。

entries.definition: the act of clearing something away
willing or arranged in a certain way
a usual tendency of mind
to throw something away
to put something in the rubbish
to make someone tend toward something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a box at the door and end with a settled matter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的旧箱子开始，落到一件被了结的事。

normal.en: Dis- plus pose: things are set apart and settled.
normal.cn: dis 加 pose，把东西分开摆好并了结。

normal.en: A cleared room disposes of a hundred small doubts.
normal.cn: 清空的房间，处理掉一百个小疑虑。

normal.en: Dispose of waste before it disposes of the garden.
normal.cn: 趁垃圾还没毁掉花园，先处理掉它。

normal.en: A kind host disposes a guest to stay longer.
normal.cn: 好客的主人让客人愿意多坐一会。

normal.en: Disposed to help, she opened the door at once.
normal.cn: 她有意帮忙，立刻开了门。

abstract.en: Picture a box carried out and set on the step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被搬出去放在台阶上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand brushing dust from an empty shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把空架上的灰拂掉。

abstract.en: Picture a chair turned slightly toward the fire.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子微微转向炉火。

examples.en: They disposed of the old files before moving.
examples.cn: 搬家前他们把旧文件处理掉了。

examples.en: The warm welcome disposed her to stay.
examples.cn: 热情的欢迎使她愿意留下。

examples.en: Please dispose of your rubbish properly.
examples.cn: 请妥善处理你的垃圾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dispose 记成「分开摆好」：dis 是分开，pos 是放置，把东西分开放好，该留的留，该清的清，就是处理。

root: 源自拉丁语 disponere（分置、安排），由 dis-（分开）与 ponere（放置）组成，经古法语 disposer 进入英语。本义是把东西各自摆好，后来引申为把不要的东西清出去，也指把心思摆向某一方。

sensesIntro.en: From setting each thing in its place to leaning a mind toward a choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把每样东西各就其位，到让心思偏向一个选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old box carried to the door and an empty corner behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧箱子被搬到门口，身后是一块空角落。

branches.en: The first sense is the sorting that ends in a bin.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是终于进了垃圾桶的分拣。

branches.en: The second sense is the sorting of a mind.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是心思的分拣。

branches.en: Both senses begin by placing things apart.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从把东西分开放开始。

branches.en: Both leave the space clearer than before.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让空间比原先清爽。

branches.en: Only the second sense happens without hands.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项不用动手。

intro.en: Dispose belongs to the Latin ponere family, with disposal, disposition and predispose around it.
intro.cn: dispose 属于拉丁语 ponere 一族，周围有 disposal、disposition 与 predispose。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, to place, gives disponere and dispose, and the prefix marks setting things apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere（放置）给出 disponere 与 dispose，前缀标出把东西分开摆放。

items.meaning: to set out or get rid of
items.example: They disposed of the boxes at noon.
items.exampleCN: 他们中午把箱子处理掉了。

items.example: Disposal of the waste took a week.
items.exampleCN: 处理这些废物用了一周。

items.example: A disposable plate bent in his hand.
items.exampleCN: 一只一次性盘子在他手里弯了。

items.example: A quiet disposition suited the work.
items.exampleCN: 安静的性情适合这份工作。

items.example: Cold rooms predispose people to colds.

definition_zh: 标签；贴标签；捉人游戏
definition_en: a small label fixed to something, or to fix such a label
core_image: 行李牌系在箱子的把手上
scene: 她把写有名字的行李牌系在箱子上。 She tied a name tag to the handle of her suitcase.
sceneCN: 这里 tag 是「标签」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把写有名字的行李牌系在行李箱把手上。

senses.title: A small attached label
senses.definition: a small piece of paper or plastic fixed to something to identify it
senses.definitionCN: 系在或贴在物品上用于识别的小纸片或塑料片
senses.example: She tied a name tag to the handle of her suitcase.
senses.exampleCN: 她把姓名牌系在行李箱把手上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a hanging piece of cloth used as a mark.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是垂下来作记号的小布片，今天的标签沿用了这个「挂着的小片」形象。

senses.title: To mark with a label
senses.definition: to attach a label to something or mark it for identification
senses.definitionCN: 给某物贴上标签或加上标识
senses.example: The staff tagged every bag before loading.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员在装车前给每个包贴上标签。
senses.why: The noun turned into the act of adding the label.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转化为「加上标签」这个动作。

senses.title: A chasing playground game
senses.definition: a children's game in which one player chases and touches others
senses.definitionCN: 一名儿童追逐并触碰其他人的游戏
senses.example: The children played tag in the yard after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后孩子们在院子里玩捉人游戏。
senses.why: Touching a runner marks them, just as a tag marks an object.
senses.whyCN: 碰到跑动的人就算「标记」到他，和给物品贴标签是同一个比喻。

intro.en: Tag first meant a hanging scrap of cloth; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: tag 最早指垂下的碎布片，更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Tagge meant a hanging piece of cloth.
items.cn: tagge 指垂下的布片。

items.en: The deeper root of tagge is not settled.
items.cn: tagge 的更早词源尚无定论。

items.en: A tag became a label for identification.
items.cn: tag 变成用于识别的标签。

items.en: The verb meant to fix a label.
items.cn: 动词义为贴上标签。

items.en: The playground game borrowed the touch-and-mark idea.
items.cn: 儿童游戏借用了「触碰即标记」的想法。

note.en: Tag is set beside look-alike words and beside words for labels.
note.cn: 把 tag 与形近词以及表示标签的词作对比。

entries.definition: a small flap or strip
a torn piece of cloth
to pull hard
a piece of paper giving information
a small sign worn on clothes
a small adhesive label

normalIntro.en: A tag is a small hanging mark that says who or what something is.
normalIntro.cn: tag 是一片挂着的小标记，说明这是谁的、这是什么。

normal.en: She tied a name tag to her suitcase.
normal.cn: 她把姓名牌系在行李箱上。

normal.en: The staff tagged every bag before loading.
normal.cn: 工作人员在装车前给每个包贴上标签。

normal.en: The children played tag in the yard.
normal.cn: 孩子们在院子里玩捉人游戏。

normal.en: Check the price tag before you buy.
normal.cn: 买之前看看价签。

normal.en: He tagged along with his older brother.
normal.cn: 他跟着哥哥一起走。

abstract.en: A tag is a name that hangs on a thing.
abstract.cn: 标签是挂在一件东西上的名字。

abstract.en: To touch is to mark, in games and in labels.
abstract.cn: 触碰就是标记，游戏和标签里都一样。

abstract.en: Small cloth, lasting identity.
abstract.cn: 小小布片，留下身份。

examples.en: She tied a name tag to the handle of her suitcase.
examples.cn: 她把姓名牌系在行李箱把手上。

examples.en: The staff tagged every bag before loading.
examples.cn: 工作人员在装车前给每个包贴上标签。

examples.en: The children played tag in the yard after school.
examples.cn: 放学后孩子们在院子里玩捉人游戏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贴个」——把标签「贴个」在箱子上，一眼就认出是谁的行李。

root: 中古英语 tagge 指垂下的布片，词源不确定，一般认为与「悬挂的小片」这一形象有关。

sensesIntro.en: Tag runs from a hanging cloth mark to a label, the act of labelling, and a touching game.
sensesIntro.cn: tag 从垂下的布片标记，延伸到标签、贴标签的动作，以及触碰即算的儿童游戏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cloth mark swinging from a handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在把手上晃动着的小布片。

branches.en: A label names what it hangs on.
branches.cn: 标签为所挂之物命名。

branches.en: The act of adding the label.
branches.cn: 这是加上标签的动作。

branches.en: Touching a runner marks them.
branches.cn: 碰到奔跑的人就算标记成功。

branches.en: Noun and verb share one image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共用一个形象。

branches.en: A price tag speaks without words.
branches.cn: 价签不必说话就传达了信息。

intro.en: Tag forms a small modern family through compounding.
intro.cn: tag 通过复合构词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Tag is Middle English with an uncertain root, so Latin parallels are only semantic.
latinIntro.cn: tag 属中古英语且词根不确定，拉丁语中只有语义对应词。

items.example: The tags are on the bags.
