definition_zh: 看不见的；无形的；不受注意的
definition_en: not able to be seen because it is too small, too far, clear, or simply unnoticed
core_image: 一块玻璃立在空地上，人一走过去就消失在里面
scene: 实验台上一支玻璃管里冒气，肉眼什么都看不出来。 The gas is invisible, but it turns the litmus paper blue.
sceneCN: 这里 invisible 是「看不见的」（第 1 个义项：眼睛无法察觉），句意为这种气体看不见，却能让蓝色石蕊试纸变色。画面里的物件：玻璃管、石蕊试纸、手套。

pos.zh: 形容词：看不见的；无形的；不受注意的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「隐形；不可见性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「无形地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看得见的」
同带 vis- 词根的形近词，义为「视力；远见」

senses.title: Cannot be seen
senses.definition: impossible for the eye to notice because of size, distance, or colourlessness
senses.definitionCN: 因为太小、太远或没有颜色而无法被眼睛察觉
senses.example: The bacteria are invisible without a microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 没有显微镜，这些细菌是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre meant "to see"; in- negatives the verb visibilis comes from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看见」，in- 把 visibilis 所自的动词否定掉。

senses.title: Wrongly ignored
senses.definition: present but not noticed or counted by people who should care
senses.definitionCN: 实际存在却被本该关心的人忽略或不算在内
senses.example: Older carers often feel invisible to the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的照护者常觉得在医疗体系里没人看见他们。
senses.why: Social use takes the eye metaphor into institutions: what is not counted is not seen.
senses.whyCN: 社会用法把眼睛的比喻带进制度：没被统计的，就等于没被看见。

senses.title: Not obvious in money or power
senses.definition: hidden in form but real in effect, like costs or forces
senses.definitionCN: 形式上隐藏、实际却有效果，如成本或力量
senses.example: Every purchase carries invisible costs for the river.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次购买都为这条河带来看不见的代价。
senses.why: Accounts talk about invisible balances when the effect is real but the form is not on the page.
senses.whyCN: 账目里的「无形」余额，说的是效果真实、却不写在纸面上。

intro.en: Invisible is Latin in- "not" plus visibilis, "that can be seen", from videre "to see".
intro.cn: invisible 是拉丁 in-「不」加 visibilis「可见的」，后者来自 videre「看」。

items.en: videre meant "to see".
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」。

items.en: visibilis meant "able to be seen".
items.cn: visibilis 意为「能被看见的」。

items.en: in- negated it to invisibilis, "not visible".
items.cn: in- 将其否定为 invisibilis「看不见的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into English forms.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带入英语形式。

items.en: Science and economics borrowed it for gases, germs, and hidden costs.
items.cn: 科学与经济学借它说气体、细菌与隐性成本。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis- root; the near-meaning group holds words for what cannot be noticed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis- 词根；近义组收表示无法察觉的词。

entries.definition: Able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「可见的」，只少否定前缀。

entries.definition: Impossible to defeat.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可战胜的」，拼写只差两个字母。

entries.definition: Related to sight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「视觉的」，同词根。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「隐藏的」，多为有意。

entries.definition: Not noticed by anyone watching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「未被看见的」，偏观察角度。

entries.definition: Real but impossible to touch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「无形的」，强调摸不着。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word tied to the small prefix that says no.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它系在那个表示「不」的小前缀上。

normal.en: in- says not, and visible says able to be seen.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，visible 是「能被看见」。

normal.en: Glass is visible only by its edge.
normal.cn: 玻璃只有靠边缘才看得出来。

normal.en: Invisible ink has to be warmed to show up.
normal.cn: 隐形墨水要加热才显现。

normal.en: Remove in- and the word turns into its exact opposite.
normal.cn: 去掉 in-，这个词就变成它的正相反。

normal.en: A person can be invisible without vanishing.
normal.cn: 人可以不消失，却「不被看见」。

abstract.en: Invisibility is a matter of who is looking, not only of what is there.
abstract.cn: 无形不只取决于有没有东西，还取决于谁在看。

abstract.en: Some costs never appear on the receipt.
abstract.cn: 有些代价永远不会出现在小票上。

abstract.en: The ignored are the truest invisible ones.
abstract.cn: 被忽略的人，才是最彻底的无形。

examples.en: Ultraviolet light is invisible but burns the skin.
examples.cn: 紫外线看不见，却会晒伤皮肤。

examples.en: The seam was made invisible with tiny stitches.
examples.cn: 那道缝用极细的针脚做成了看不见的。

examples.en: Cleaners work at night and stay invisible to most staff.
examples.cn: 保洁员夜里工作，对大多数员工来说一直「看不见」。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ vis（看）+ ible（能……的）——看不到的

root: 拉丁语 in-「不」+ videre「看」→ visibilis「可见的」→ invisibilis → 英语 invisible。同族有 visible、vision、visual、invisibility。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: hidden from the eye, ignored by people, and real but not obvious.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：肉眼看不见、被人忽视，以及真实却不显形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is there, but the eye slides past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：东西就在那里，眼睛却滑过去了。

branches.en: THE GLASS: clear things that show only at the edge.
branches.cn: 玻璃这条线：只在边缘显形的透明物。

branches.en: THE COUNT: people left out of the numbers.
branches.cn: 统计这条线：被数字落下的人。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: forces with real weight and no line on the page.
branches.cn: 账本这条线：真有分量却没有条目的力量。

branches.en: THE EYE: both senses depend on someone failing to notice.
branches.cn: 眼睛这条线：两个义项都取决于有人没留意到。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: institutions decide what becomes visible.
branches.cn: 制度这条线：是制度决定什么能被看见。

intro.en: Invisible is in- "not", vis- "see", and -ible "able to be".
intro.cn: invisible 是 in-「不」、vis-「看」与 -ible「能被……的」三段。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and invisibilis are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 invisibilis 均有记载。

items.example: It flips visible into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它把 visible 翻成反义。

items.example: The root also appears in vision and visual.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 vision 与 visual。

items.example: It forms visible, able to be seen.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 visible，能被看见的。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.meaning: sight or a plan seen ahead

items.example: Same root with an adjective ending.

definition_zh: 可预测的；可预料的；意料之中的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的
definition_en: able to be known or stated in advance; happening as everyone already expects; too regular to be interesting; and steady enough to be relied on
core_image: 老人的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，节拍一下都不差
scene: 老朋友聚会，话题总是从天气开始，再绕回谁又长胖了、谁换了工作。 The conversation followed its predictable course: weather first, then who had gained weight.
sceneCN: 这里 predictable 指「可预料的、不出所料的」（第 2 个义项：事情按大家预想的样子发生）；句意为谈话照着可以预料的路子走：先说天气，再说谁胖了。图中可辨识场景：围坐的老朋友、从天气开头的话题、彼此打趣的笑声。

pos.zh: 可预测的；可预料的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 praedicere 经英语改造而来，义为「预言；预测」
由 predict 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「预言；预测」
由 predictable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可预测性」
由否定前缀 un- 与 predictable 复合而成，义为「不可预测的」

senses.title: Able to be stated in advance
senses.titleCN: 可预测的；可以预先断定的
senses.definition: able to be known or worked out in advance because the evidence or the pattern allows it
senses.definitionCN: 因为证据或规律足够，所以能够提前知道或推算出来
senses.example: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。
senses.why: Latin praedicere meant to say something beforehand, and -able turns that act into a possibility: whatever can be said before it happens is predictable.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praedicere 意为「预先说出」，-able 把这个动作变成一种可能性：凡能在发生之前被说出来的，就是可预测的。

senses.title: Happening as everyone already expects
senses.titleCN: 意料之中的；不出所料的
senses.definition: happening in the way most people already expect, so that it causes no surprise when it does
senses.definitionCN: 按多数人早已预想的样子发生，真的发生时谁都不觉意外
senses.example: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。
senses.why: If a thing can be said before it happens, then when it happens nobody is surprised; the sense slides from what can be foretold to what is simply unsurprising.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能在发生前被说出来，它真的发生时谁也不会吃惊；词义就从「可以预言」滑到「本来就没什么意外」。

senses.title: Too regular to be interesting
senses.definition: too regular or conventional to hold interest, showing no invention and no surprise
senses.definitionCN: 过于规律或循规蹈矩，因而提不起兴趣，既无新意也无意外
senses.example: Critics called the sequel predictable and safe.
senses.exampleCN: 评论界说这部续集平淡无趣、四平八稳。
senses.why: A pattern regular enough to be foretold soon becomes a pattern with nothing new inside it, and the same adjective turns into mild blame.
senses.whyCN: 一个规律到能被预言的格局，很快就变成内里没有新东西的格局，同一个形容词于是带上轻微的责备。

senses.title: Steady enough to be relied on
senses.definition: of a supply, income or person: behaving in a steady way that plans can be built on
senses.definitionCN: 指供给、收入或人行为稳定，可以照着它做计划
senses.example: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water to a lucky season.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农户更想要稳定的供水，而不是碰运气的丰水季。
senses.why: When the certainty is useful rather than boring, the word becomes praise: a predictable supply is one that a plan can be built on.
senses.whyCN: 当这种确定性是有用的而不是无聊的，这个词就变成称赞：可预测的供给，就是能照着它做计划的供给。

intro.en: Predictable is predict plus -able. The Latin verb behind predict meant to say a thing beforehand, and English first used it for declaring rather than for foretelling.
intro.cn: predictable 是 predict 加 -able。predict 背后的拉丁动词意为「预先说出」，而英语最初用它表示宣称、断言，并非预言。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or to declare, and it stands behind a very large family of English words about speech.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣称，是英语里一大批与言语有关的词的源头。

items.en: Praedicare joined prae-, before, with dicere: to say beforehand, and also to proclaim something publicly.
items.cn: praedicare 把 prae-（在前）与 dicere 结合：预先说出，也指当众宣告。

items.en: The noun praedictio meant a foretelling or a prophecy, and it kept the solemn tone of announcing what is to come.
items.cn: 名词 praedictio 意为预言、预告，保留了宣告未来之事的庄重语气。

items.en: English predict first meant to declare or assert something, and only later settled on foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语 predict 最早意为宣称、断言某事，后来才固定为「预言未来」。

items.en: The adjective was formed with -able in the nineteenth century, first for events, then for people and their dull habits.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪由 -able 构成，先用于事件，随后用于人及其乏味的习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of saying through the English family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what can be counted on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「说」的拉丁动词，收它在英语里的一族词；近义组收表示「可以指望」的形容词。

entries.definition: To say what will happen before it does.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前说出它会发生。

entries.definition: A statement about what will happen in the future.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将来会发生什么的说法；预言。

entries.definition: Impossible to know in advance, often changing without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 无法提前知道的；常指变化无常。

entries.definition: The quality of being able to be known in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 可以提前知道的性质；可预测性。

entries.definition: Able to be known or expected in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 能够提前知道或料到的。

entries.definition: Thought likely to happen or to be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为很可能发生或属实的。

entries.definition: Following a fixed pattern, with equal gaps between events.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定规律出现的；间隔均匀的。

entries.definition: Ordinary, repeated and part of the usual order of things.
entries.definitionCN: 平常而反复的，属于常规安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of saying beforehand, so its centre is speech: what can be said in advance, and then what has nothing left to say.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「预先说出」的拉丁动词上，中心是「说」：能提前说出来的，以及后来没什么可说的。

normal.en: Dicere is to say and prae- is before, so predict is literally to say before, and -able makes it possible to do so.
normal.cn: dicere 是说，prae- 是在前，所以 predict 字面就是「预先说」，-able 让它成为「可以预先说的」。

normal.en: Prediction is the noun in -ion, and it can be a weather forecast or a prophecy.
normal.cn: prediction 是加 -ion 的名词，可以是天气预报，也可以是预言。

normal.en: Unpredictable adds un-, and it is the word used for weather, toddlers and market prices.
normal.cn: unpredictable 加了否定前缀 un-，天气、幼儿和市场价格都常被这样形容。

normal.en: Predictability names the quality, and planners pay for it in supply chains.
normal.cn: predictability 指这种性质，供应链上的规划者愿意为它花钱。

normal.en: Predictable income is praise, predictable plot is blame: the same word, two directions of judgement.
normal.cn: predictable income 是称赞，predictable plot 是贬斥：同一个词，两个方向的评价。

abstract.en: To predict is to speak before the event; to be predictable is to leave the future no room to speak.
abstract.cn: predict 是在事情之前说话；predictable 则是不给未来留下说话的空间。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between what we know and what happens, and that distance can be comfort or boredom.
abstract.cn: 这个词量的是「我们所知」与「实际发生」之间的距离，而这段距离可以是安心，也可以是无聊。

abstract.en: A predictable world is easy to live in and hard to be surprised by, and the adjective holds both halves.
abstract.cn: 可预测的世界住起来省心，却很难再有惊喜，这个形容词把两半都装着。

examples.en: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
examples.cn: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。

examples.en: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
examples.cn: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。

examples.en: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water.
examples.cn: 这里的农户更喜欢稳定的供水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞迪克特波」——提前把话说明白，事情照着走；predictable 就是可预测的。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ dicere（说）→ praedicere（预先说出）→ 名词 praedictio（预言）→ 英语 predict → 加 -able 成 predictable。同族有 prediction、unpredictable。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move along one line: what can be said in advance, what therefore surprises nobody, what becomes dull through repetition, and what is steady enough to build a plan on.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着一条线移动：能提前说出的，因此谁都不意外的，因重复而变得乏味的，以及稳定到可以据之做计划的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old hand tapping the table in the same rhythm, beat after beat, without one missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只苍老的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，一下接一下，一次不差。

branches.en: a tide table marked to the minute
branches.cn: 精确到分钟的潮汐表

branches.en: an audience guessing the ending before it comes
branches.cn: 观众在结局到来前就猜到了

branches.en: a sequel that repeats every turn of the first film
branches.cn: 把第一部每个转折都重来一遍的续集

branches.en: an irrigation channel running on schedule
branches.cn: 按日程放水的灌溉渠

branches.en: a forecast and a supply both trusted enough to plan with
branches.cn: 一份预报与一份供给都可靠到能据之做计划

intro.en: A Latin verb of saying and a prefix meaning before make the verb; English -able then turns the act of foretelling into a quality, and -ity and un- extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「说」的拉丁动词和一个表示「在前」的前缀造出动词；英语的 -able 再把「预言」这个动作变成性质，-ity 与 un- 又扩展了这一族。

latinIntro.en: Dicere, praedicere and praedictio are all recorded Latin forms, so the family is documented rather than reconstructed; only the English adjective is recent.
latinIntro.cn: dicere、praedicere 与 praedictio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，所以这一族词有据可查，并非重构；只有英语形容词是较晚才有的。

definition_zh: 博士的；博士学位的；博士研究的
definition_en: relating to a doctorate, the highest university degree, or to the research and students connected with it
core_image: 一顶博士帽压在一摞改过无数遍的论文上
scene: 答辩室的灯亮到深夜，桌上摊着改得密密麻麻的稿子。 She finally finished her doctoral dissertation after six years of fieldwork.
sceneCN: 这里 doctoral 是「博士研究的」（第 2 个义项：与博士论文和博士研究有关）；句意是她做了六年田野调查后终于完成了博士论文。

pos.zh: 形容词：博士的；博士学位的；博士研究的

derivatives.zh: 由 doctor 加名词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「博士学位」
由前缀 post-「之后」加 doctoral 构成，义为「博士后的」

senses.title: Relating to a doctorate
senses.definition: relating to the highest university degree, which is awarded after original research
senses.definitionCN: 与最高一级大学学位有关的，该学位须在原创研究之后授予
senses.example: A doctoral degree usually takes at least three years.
senses.exampleCN: 博士学位通常至少需要三年。
senses.why: Latin doctor meant teacher, and the suffix -al turns that title into an adjective of belonging, so the degree is named after the teacher it certifies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 doctor 是「教师」，后缀 -al 把这个称号变成表示归属的形容词；这个学位正是以它所要认证的教师身份来命名的。

senses.title: Relating to dissertation research
senses.definition: connected with the original research and dissertation required for a doctorate
senses.definitionCN: 与取得博士学位所需的原创研究和学位论文有关的
senses.example: Her doctoral work examined how coastal soils change over time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的博士研究工作考察了沿海土壤随时间发生的变化。
senses.why: Research is the substance of the degree, so the same adjective naturally describes the long investigation behind the thesis.
senses.whyCN: 研究是这一学位的实质内容，因此同一个形容词自然也能描述论文背后那场漫长的调查。

senses.title: Relating to a doctoral candidate
senses.definition: used to describe a student who is working toward a doctorate
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述正在攻读博士学位的学生
senses.example: Doctoral candidates must defend their findings before a committee.
senses.exampleCN: 博士生必须在委员会面前为自己的研究成果答辩。
senses.why: The person is named after the degree still being earned, so one adjective covers both the title and the reader for it.
senses.whyCN: 人是以尚未到手的学位来命名的，所以同一个形容词既能修饰学位，也能修饰正在攻读它的人。

intro.en: Doctoral is built on Latin doctor, a teacher, plus the English adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: doctoral 由拉丁语 doctor（教师）加英语形容词后缀 -al 构成。

items.en: The teaching verb behind Latin docere is usually traced to a root meaning to take or accept; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 docere 背后的「教」义一般追溯到表示「拿取、接受」的词根，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Docere meant to teach or to show, and it also produced doctrina, teaching, and doctor.
items.cn: docere 意为「教、示范」，它还生出 doctrina（教导）与 doctor。

items.en: Doctor was an agent noun meaning teacher, and in the universities it became a title for a learned master.
items.cn: doctor 是施事名词，意为「教师」；在大学里逐渐成为博学之士的头衔。

items.en: Doctoratus named the degree of a doctor; the earliest university records are from the thirteenth century, though exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: doctoratus 指博士的学位；最早的大学记录出现在十三世纪，确切年代仍有争议。

items.en: English formed doctoral from doctor plus -al to describe anything belonging to the degree.
items.cn: 英语用 doctor 加 -al 造出 doctoral，用来描述属于这一学位的事物。

items.en: The adjective spread from degrees to dissertations, research projects and candidates.
items.cn: 这个形容词从学位扩展到论文、研究项目以及在读的候选人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin teaching root; the near-meaning group gathers other academic labels.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「教」这个词根；近义组收的是其他学术称谓。

entries.definition: A person holding the highest university degree, or a medical practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指拥有最高大学学位的人，也指医生；与 doctoral 同出拉丁语 docere。

entries.definition: The degree itself, formed from doctor with the noun suffix -ate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「博士学位」，由 doctor 加名词后缀 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: Describing research done after a doctorate has been awarded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「博士后的」，指取得博士学位之后所做的研究。

entries.definition: A student or course above the first degree level; broader than doctoral.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「研究生、研究生的」，范围比 doctoral 更宽。

entries.definition: Relating to universities and scholarly study in general.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术的、大学的」，泛指高校与学术研究。

entries.definition: Showing careful academic study and knowledge; it describes style, not a degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有学者风范的、博学的」，描述风格而非学位层级。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin family of docere, to teach, and show where each form fits.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁词族 docere（教）展开，并说明每个形式的位置。

normal.en: Docere means to teach; every word in this family starts from a classroom.
normal.cn: docere 意为「教」，这一族的每个词都从课堂出发。

normal.en: Doctor was first a teacher, then a learned title, and only later a medical doctor.
normal.cn: doctor 先是教师，后来成为博学头衔，最后才常指医生。

normal.en: Doctorate is the degree, so doctoral describes what belongs to that degree.
normal.cn: doctorate 是学位本身，doctoral 则描述属于这个学位的事物。

normal.en: The suffix -al simply means relating to, as in doctoral research.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 只表示「与……有关」，如 doctoral research 中的用法。

normal.en: Post- means after, so postdoctoral work begins once the degree is in hand.
normal.cn: post- 表示「之后」，所以 postdoctoral 指拿到学位之后的研究。

abstract.cn: 想象一顶方形博士帽压在一摞改过无数遍的纸页上。

abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，一位候选人在灯下答辩到深夜。

examples.en: She is writing her doctoral thesis on ancient soils.
examples.cn: 她正在写关于古代土壤的博士论文。

examples.en: The laboratory offers places for doctoral students from abroad.
examples.cn: 这个实验室为来自海外的博士生提供名额。

examples.en: His doctoral research was published as a short book.
examples.cn: 他的博士研究被出版成了一本小书。

root: 由拉丁语 docere（教、示范）派生：docere 生出 doctor（教师）与 doctrina（教导），中世纪拉丁语 doctoratus 指博士学位，英语再以 doctor 加 -al 构成 doctoral。更早的印欧词根一般追溯到表示「拿取、接受」的形式，更深的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective covers the degree, the research behind it and the person still working for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形容词覆盖了学位本身、支撑学位的论文研究，以及仍在攻读的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square cap placed on a tall pile of revised pages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶方形博士帽放在一摞改过多遍的纸页上。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: doctoral names what belongs to the doctorate itself.
branches.cn: 学位线：doctoral 指属于博士学位本身的事物。

branches.en: THE WORK: the adjective also names the research and dissertation that earn the degree.
branches.cn: 研究线：这个形容词也指为取得学位而做的研究与论文。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a candidate carries the adjective of the degree still being earned.
branches.cn: 人物线：在读的候选人带着那个尚未到手的学位的形容词。

branches.en: Degree and research share one label because the degree is defined by the research.
branches.cn: 学位与研究共用一个标签，因为学位正是由研究来定义的。

branches.en: The same word describes the thesis and the person writing it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能描述论文，也能描述写论文的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin docere, doctor and doctrina are recorded; doctoratus belongs to medieval university Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 docere、doctor 与 doctrina 均有文献记录；doctoratus 属中世纪大学拉丁语。

definition_zh: 同情的；赞同的；体贴的
definition_en: showing that you understand and care about someone else s trouble
core_image: 朋友低声听着，眉头跟着对方一起皱起
scene: 听完她的遭遇，朋友们都很同情。 Her friends were sympathetic when they heard her story.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathetic 是「同情的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：听完她的遭遇，朋友们都很同情。

senses.title: Feeling for someone in trouble
senses.definition: showing care about another person s suffering
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的痛苦表示关心
senses.example: Her friends were sympathetic when they heard her story.
senses.exampleCN: 听完她的遭遇，朋友们都很同情。
senses.why: The Greek root means sharing feeling, so the adjective names feeling alongside another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为共同感受，因此这个形容词指与他人一同感受。

senses.title: Favourable to an idea
senses.definition: willing to support a plan or view
senses.definitionCN: 愿意支持某个计划或观点
senses.example: The committee was sympathetic to the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会赞同这项提议。
senses.why: Sharing another person s feeling extends to sharing their view.
senses.whyCN: 与他人共感会延伸到认同他们的看法。

senses.title: Kind and considerate
senses.definition: gentle in the way you treat others
senses.definitionCN: 待人温和周到
senses.example: The nurse gave a sympathetic smile.
senses.exampleCN: 护士体贴地笑了笑。
senses.why: A person who feels with you will usually act gently, so the word also means considerate.
senses.whyCN: 能与你共感的人通常会温和行事，于是这个词也表示体贴。

intro.en: Sympathetic joins Greek syn, together, with pathos, feeling.
intro.cn: sympathetic 由希腊语 syn（共同）与 pathos（感受）组合而成。

items.en: Sympatheia meant fellow feeling.
items.cn: sympatheia 意为共同的感受。

items.en: Pathos meant what is felt or suffered.
items.cn: pathos 意为所感或所受。

items.en: Late Latin sympathia named shared feeling.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 sympathia 指共同的感受。

items.en: Sympathetic first described natural harmony between things.
items.cn: sympathetic 最初描述事物之间的天然共鸣。

items.en: Sympathetic narrowed to caring about another s trouble.
items.cn: sympathetic 收窄为关心他人疾苦。

note.en: Sympathetic is compared with look-alike words and with words for caring.
note.cn: 把 sympathetic 与形近词以及表示关怀的词作比较。
